answer.answerText:
**No—on the stated tables-and-chairs arrangement, it does not need to be classified as Group A-3 if it is an assembly space accessory to the apartment-building occupancy.** Table 1004.1.3 assigns an assembly-without-fixed-seats, unconcentrated (tables and chairs) factor of 15 net square feet per occupant. At 900 net square feet, the calculated occupant load is 900 ÷ 15 = **60 occupants**, fewer than 75. An accessory assembly room with an occupant load below 75 must be classified as Group B or as part of the occupancy it serves, although its plumbing fixtures may be calculated under the assembly requirements (BC §§ 1004.1.3, 303.1.3).

Group A-3 otherwise includes recreation, amusement, and other assembly uses not classified elsewhere in Group A (BC § 303.4). The fact that use is limited to residents supports the stated residential-amenity context but does not by itself establish the required legal accessory relationship. If the room is not accessory, BC § 303.1.2 separately classifies a **building or nonaccessory tenant space** used for assembly purposes with fewer than 75 occupants as Group B; that provision does not itself expressly address a standalone nonaccessory room.

The classification must account for every intended use, not merely its normal furniture layout. If the room will also be used in an arrangement or for an activity producing an occupant load of 75 or more, or for a different purpose, the classification must be reevaluated for that use (BC § 302.1).

answer.answerText:
**Yes.** If the multipurpose room is validly classified as Group B, PC Table 403.1 supplies the normal Group B fixture requirements because fixture minimums are based on the Building Code occupancy classification and occupant load. (PC § 403.1)

The fewer-than-75 Assembly provisions also create a permitted **alternative** Assembly calculation; they do not state that the normal Group B table row is unavailable:

| Classification path | Fixture-calculation result |
|---|---|
| Room is accessory to another occupancy and used for Assembly purposes by fewer than 75 persons | It may be classified as Group B or as part of the occupancy served, and its fixtures are permitted to be calculated under Assembly requirements. (BC § 303.1.3) |
| Building or nonaccessory tenant space used for Assembly purposes by fewer than 75 persons | It is classified as Group B, and its fixtures are permitted to be calculated under Assembly requirements. (BC § 303.1.2; PC § 403.1, Table 403.1 note j) |

Thus, for a valid Group B classification, the normal Group B row is a usable baseline; the Assembly ratios are also expressly permitted for either of the above fewer-than-75 Assembly paths. The final fixture count still requires the Building Code occupant load and the applicable Table 403.1 ratios. Divide the load equally between sexes unless approved statistical data supports another distribution; apply the ratios by fixture type; round fractions up; and, for multiple occupancies, sum fractional results before rounding. (PC §§ 403.1, 403.1.1)

If relevant to the eventual count, fixtures in a family or assisted-use toilet/bathing room required by BC § 1109.2.1 may count for either sex in an Assembly calculation; fixtures in single-occupant toilet rooms may also count for either sex, except that fixtures counted under the PC § 403.2.1 exception may count only for that sex. (PC §§ 403.1.2, 403.1.3)

The unresolved classification-path fact is whether this room is accessory to another occupancy or instead is within a building or nonaccessory tenant space. That fact determines which BC provision supports the Assembly-calculation alternative, although both supplied paths permit that alternative.

supportedPoints.heading: Group B classification uses the Group B fixture row
supportedPoints.explanation: PC Section 403.1 requires plumbing fixtures by occupancy type and in the Table 403.1 minimum numbers; the Building Code determines occupant load and occupancy classification. Accordingly, where the room is validly classified as Group B, the Group B row supplies the ordinary fixture calculation baseline.

supportedPoints.heading: Accessory Assembly room may use Assembly fixture requirements
supportedPoints.explanation: A room or space used for Assembly purposes, with fewer than 75 occupants, and accessory to another occupancy is classified as Group B or as part of the occupancy served. Its fixture count is permitted to be calculated using the Assembly requirements.

supportedPoints.heading: Nonaccessory Assembly building or tenant space may use Assembly fixture requirements
supportedPoints.explanation: A building or nonaccessory tenant space used for Assembly purposes by fewer than 75 persons is classified as Group B, and its fixtures are permitted to be calculated using Assembly requirements. PC Table 403.1 note j states the same expressly limited Assembly-calculation permission.

supportedPoints.heading: Fixture calculation and rounding method
supportedPoints.explanation: The total occupant load is divided equally between sexes unless approved statistical data establishes another distribution. Apply each fixture ratio by fixture type to each sex and round fractions up; where multiple occupancies are involved, sum the fractional results for each occupancy before rounding up.

supportedPoints.heading: Conditional credits for certain toilet rooms
supportedPoints.explanation: Fixtures in family or assisted-use toilet and bathing rooms required by BC Section 1109.2.1 may count toward either sex in Assembly occupancies. Fixtures in single-occupant toilet rooms may count toward either sex, except fixtures in toilet rooms subject to the PC Section 403.2.1 exception may count only for the applicable sex.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 403.1.1 403.1.1 Fixture calculations. To determine the occupant load of each sex, the total occupant load shall be divided in half. To determine the required number of fixtures, the fixture ratio or ratios for each fixture type shall be applied to the occupant load of each sex in accordance with Table 403.1 . Fractional numbers resulting from applying the fixture ratios of Table 403.1 shall be rounded up to the next whole number. Fixture calculations in Group B office occupancies shall utilize the total occupant load on a given floor to determine the number of fixtures required for that floor. To determine the required number of fixtures, the fixture ratio or ratios for each fixture type shall be applied to the occupant load of each sex in accordance with Table 403.1 . Fractional numbers resulting from applying the fixture ratios of Table 403.1 shall be rounded up to the next whole number. For calculations involving multiple occupancies, such fractional numbers for each occupancy shall first be summed and then rounded up to the next whole number. The number of plumbing fixtures located within the required public toilet facilities shall be provided in accordance with Section 403 for all customers, patrons and visitors. Employee and public toilet facilities may be separate or combined. Where combined facilities are provided, the number of plumbing fixtures shall be in accordance with Section 403 for all users.
